name: How do I compare bathroom remodeling bids fairly?

mainEntity.name: What should be included in a bathroom remodeling bid so I can compare quotes fairly?
mainEntity.text: What should be included in a bathroom remodeling bid so I can compare quotes fairly?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bathroom bids are hard to compare when one contractor uses a broad lump sum and another lists every line item. To compare them fairly, ask each contractor to spell out demolition, waterproofing, plumbing, electrical, tile setting, fixtures, drywall, painting, permit handling, debris removal, and final cleanup. The bid should also identify what materials are included and what is excluded, such as specialty tile, glass doors, custom cabinets, or unexpected subfloor repair. A lower price is not always better if it omits labor or assumes unrealistically simple conditions. The best bids are detailed enough that you can see where your money is going and where change orders might happen. If a proposal is vague, ask for revisions before choosing the contractor.
acceptedAnswer.description: A fair bathroom remodeling bid should clearly list demolition, waterproofing, plumbing, electrical, tile, fixtures, drywall, painting, permits, and cleanup. If one quote is much lower, it may be missing important items or using lower-grade materials.
